title: Self-Contained Euclidean Step Counter
content: euclideanSteps a b counts the division steps of the Euclidean algorithm by well-founded recursion on b: zero when b = 0, else euclideanSteps b (a % b) + 1. The entry defines its own counter (rather than importing the parent's) so the uniqueness argument stands alone; the accompanying unfolding lemma euclideanSteps_pos_eq exposes the recursion for a positive second argument.

title: Two-Sided Lamé Bound (Proof Engine)
content: The single engine driving every result: by strong induction on the step count n, a pair (a, b) with b > 0 taking n steps satisfies fib(n+1) ≤ b AND (for n ≥ 2) the one-level-down remainder bound fib n ≤ a % b. Returning both bounds at once is what makes the forcing possible — the remainder bound on a % b is exactly the extra inequality needed to trap b from above once a is pinned.
mathContext: $\operatorname{steps}(a,b)=n \wedge b>0 \implies F_{n+1} \le b \ \wedge\ (n \ge 2 \implies F_n \le a \bmod b)$.

title: Fibonacci Pair Achieves n Steps
content: The reverse inclusion: euclideanSteps(fib(n+2), fib(n+1)) = n for n ≥ 1. Induction from the base (fib 3, fib 2) = (2, 1), using the Fibonacci mod identity fib(n+2) % fib(n+1) = fib n so each Euclidean step descends one Fibonacci index. This certifies the Fibonacci pair really is n-step, so the characterisation's singleton is non-empty.

title: The a-Side Lamé Bound
content: The larger input is bounded below by fib(n+2): if (a, b) takes n ≥ 1 steps with 0 < b < a then fib(n+2) ≤ a. For n = 1 the remainder vanishes so b ∣ a with a > b gives a ≥ 2b ≥ 2 = fib 3. For n ≥ 2 the two-sided bound gives fib(n+1) ≤ b and fib n ≤ a % b, which combine through a = b·(a/b) + a % b ≥ b + a % b. This is the bound whose equality case the uniqueness theorem analyses.

title: Forcing / Uniqueness of the Worst Case
content: The new content: if 0 < b < a takes n ≥ 1 steps and attains the minimal larger input a = fib(n+2), then b is forced to fib(n+1) exactly. With a = fib n + fib(n+1) and fib(n+1) ≤ b < a one gets a < 2b, hence a % b = a − b; the remainder bound fib n ≤ a % b then gives b ≤ fib(n+1), collapsing b to fib(n+1). So the Fibonacci pair is the unique extremal pair on the a-side — the interval [fib(n+1), fib(n+2)) contains no other n-step second input against a = fib(n+2).
mathContext: $0 < b < a \wedge \operatorname{steps}(a,b)=n \wedge a = F_{n+2} \implies b = F_{n+1}$.

title: Full Characterisation (Singleton Extremal Set)
content: Packages both directions: for n ≥ 1, the pairs (a, b) with 0 < b < a, n steps, and a = fib(n+2) are exactly {(fib(n+2), fib(n+1))}. The forward direction is worst_case_forces_fib; the reverse checks the Fibonacci pair satisfies all four constraints (n steps via euclideanSteps_fib, positivity, b < a via strict fib monotonicity, and the a-value by definition).

title: Sum Lower Bound
content: A size corollary combining both Lamé bounds: any n-step pair with 0 < b < a has a + b ≥ fib(n+3), attained by the Fibonacci pair since fib(n+2) + fib(n+1) = fib(n+3). Gives the total-input growth rate underlying the log_φ complexity bound.
mathContext: $0 < b < a \wedge \operatorname{steps}(a,b)=n \ge 1 \implies F_{n+3} \le a+b$, with equality for the Fibonacci pair.
